title: Demo · NDPS small quantity, Hindi FIR, grounds of arrest only oral
story: Accused-1, a 22-year-old student, is charged under NDPS 21(a) for 4 grams of heroin, a small quantity, so the s.37 bar does not apply; the FIR is in Hindi. He was arrested on 02.07.2026 and told the grounds of arrest only orally; the charge sheet was filed in time (day 54 of 60). The Rights Radar still shows CHECK for default bail and for the BNSS s.479 undertrial limit, because no maximum punishment was on record for the charged section, so counsel is asked to check both.

steps.title: Rights Radar
steps.caption: At intake Peshkar ran the 7 rules of the Rights Radar on the dossier as of 2026-11-14: date arithmetic and statute tables, not the language model. Default bail: CHECK, Undertrial limit (BNSS s.479): CHECK, Production within 24 hours: CHECK and Antil category: C. Each result names its rule and the dates it used; rules not yet re-checked against the bare act are marked unverified. The charge sheet came on day 54 of 60, but the radar had no maximum punishment on record, so it asks counsel to check default bail and the s.479 limit instead of ruling.

filled.label: Default bail
filled.value: CHECK: Maximum punishment is not on record, so the 60 or 90 day limit is unknown.

filled.label: Undertrial limit (BNSS s.479)
filled.value: CHECK: Maximum punishment not on record, so the threshold cannot be compared.

filled.label: Notice of appearance
filled.value: UNKNOWN: Maximum punishment is not on record.

filled.label: Grounds of arrest
filled.value: UNKNOWN: No record that the grounds of arrest were communicated.

filled.label: Production within 24 hours
filled.value: CHECK: Produced the next day; times not on record.

filled.label: Antil category
filled.value: C: Charged under a special act with stringent bail provisions (NDPS s.37): category C. Antil's categories decide how an accused who was not arrested during investigation and cooperated is treated after the charge sheet; for a client in custody this is context, not a bail entitlement.

filled.label: Statutory bar
filled.value: NOT_APPLICABLE: The NDPS section charged is a small-quantity clause, which NDPS s.37(1)(b) does not reach.

filled.value: UNANSWERED: The offence involves a commercial quantity of narcotic substance under NDPS Section 21(a), which carries a stringent punishment and is of grave nature, warranting continued custody.

filled.label: O3 against general (statutory bar)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: Section 37(1) of the NDPS Act imposes a statutory bar to grant bail, as the prosecution has not yet recorded satisfaction that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accused is not guilty.

filled.label: O4 against general (flight risk)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The applicant has been in custody for 135 days without any bail application being granted, and there is a reasonable apprehension that he may abscond if released.

filled.label: O5 against general (witness tampering)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The charge sheet has been filed and the trial is at an advanced stage; releasing the accused may lead to tampering with prosecution witnesses and influencing their testimony.

filled.label: O6 against general (antecedents)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: Although no criminal antecedents are formally recorded, the nature of the offence and the applicant's prior conduct during investigation raise concerns about his character and potential for reoffending.
